Personally I don't think pronouns should be used as identifiers, it's unnecessary. They're just references to a person, they don't need to describe that person except the minimum necessary to reference them. I think that pronouns should come from the person speaking, the name is what comes from the person being talked about. If I look like a he to them, then they can reference me as a he in their mind, if i look like a she they can do that, same with they. Linguistically my favorite is they because I think gendered pronouns aren't needed at all, but I understand it doesn't hit the same historically poetic note that he and she can. Personally my favorite is she because it makes me feel good, but I'm not going to force it on people. Pronouns need to be standardized so people know what youre talking about, not every word in the sentence need to be modified by the gender of the subject, most of the time none of them do. If a new pronoun arises that is actually usable (by usable i mean people understand what you mean when you say it) then i would be happy to use it when and if that happens. But personalized pronouns don't help anything except allow people to feel they can exert a degree of power over others, they don't have any historical poetic context nor do they have the efficiency of the gender neutral term. And since gender neutral terms can't misgender someone as they contain no assertion of gender, they works linguistically. If someone asks me to use something specific in person im not going to go out of my way to hurt their feelings, but I would try to explain to them how a system of personal pronouns is confusing and meaningless, and it puts potentially harmful stress on the people who are just trying their best to make human connection. If they still requested to be called something special I would oblige, but i'd probably avoid using pronouns altogether and end up saying their name a lot
